fullDescription:
A twelve-hour day to the Similan Islands, which sit far enough offshore that the water is a different proposition from anything closer to Krabi.

The Similans are a chain of nine granite islands in the Andaman Sea, and the distinction matters: almost everything else you snorkel in this region is limestone. Granite weathers into huge rounded boulders, above and below the waterline, so the underwater landscape is boulder fields and swim-throughs rather than coral shelf. Visibility is regularly the best in Thailand, which is why divers travel specifically for it.

The trip visits Miang Island, known as Island Four, and Ko Bangu at the northern end of the chain. Snorkelling is over shallow reef between the boulders, and the fish life is noticeably denser than on the coastal reefs because the islands are protected and further from river outflow.

The important thing to plan around: the Similan Islands close completely every year, roughly mid-October to mid-November through to April or May, under Thai national park rules that let the reef recover and account for the monsoon sea. Dates shift each year and are set by the park authority, so confirm before you build a trip around it.

Twelve hours with a long transfer at each end makes this the biggest day on the Krabi list. Motion-sensitive travellers should take something before boarding, not after.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off, the boat trip, guide, breakfast, buffet lunch, fresh fruit and drinks, and snorkelling gear.

National park fees are collected separately unless confirmed otherwise. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Granite islands, so boulder fields rather than coral shelf
Among the clearest water in Thailand
Miang Island and Ko Bangu at the north of the chain
Closed by the national park roughly November to April
Breakfast, buffet lunch, guide and snorkel gear included

fullDescription:
An eight-hour cruise capped at thirty guests, which is the number that decides what this trip actually feels like.

Most Krabi sunset boats are either a longtail carrying eight people or a day-tripper carrying a hundred. A thirty-guest cap sits in between: enough deck space to find shade or sun as you prefer, and few enough people that kayaks and paddleboards are available when you want them rather than after a queue.

The afternoon covers snorkelling, kayaking and paddleboarding among the islands off Ao Nang. Kayaks are the better way to get close to the limestone: you can paddle into the undercut bases of the karsts where the rock has been eaten away at the waterline, which a boat cannot reach.

Dinner is served on deck as the sun goes down. The limestone holds colour long after the sun is gone, so the good light lasts considerably longer here than the clock suggests.

The night swim closes the trip. Bioluminescent plankton flash when the water around them moves, so the light appears around your hands and feet. It varies genuinely night to night: darkest skies near a new moon are best, a full moon erases it, and rough water scatters it. Ask about the moon phase when you choose a date.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel transfers, the cruise with crew and guide, snorkelling equipment, kayak and paddleboard use, dinner on board, soft drinks, water and fruit, and life jackets.

Eight hours, minimum one day's notice. Bring a towel and dry clothes.
highlights: Small-group boat capped at thirty guests
Kayaks reach the undercut bases of the karsts
Snorkelling, kayaking and paddleboarding included
Dinner served on deck through sunset
Night swim among bioluminescent plankton

fullDescription:
The northern islands of Phang Nga Bay rather than the four-island circuit off Ao Nang, with a halal lunch served on board.

Koh Hong is the anchor of this route. Its draw is the lagoon: a near-enclosed pool of shallow green water ringed by limestone walls, entered through a gap that only opens to boats at certain tides. Laem Had, the sandbank on the island's northern tip, runs out into the water and changes shape with the tide, which is why no two photographs of it match.

Ko Lao Lading is the one people remember. It is a small island with a single overhanging cliff that leans out above a curve of sand, and it is the most photographed rock formation in the bay after James Bond Island. Ko Phakbia is essentially a sandbar with a fringe of trees, notable for the colour of the water around it rather than anything on land.

Snorkelling stops are chosen on the day. This stretch of bay is sheltered by islands, so it tends to stay workable when the open sea towards Phi Phi is rough.

A halal meal is provided as standard rather than on request, which is worth knowing if that is a consideration for your group.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers round-trip hotel transfer, national park fees, snorkelling equipment, the halal meal, fruit and drinks, and a local guide. National park fees being included here is unusual on this coast, so this price is closer to all-in than most.

Six hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Koh Hong lagoon, entered only at certain tides
Laem Had sandbank, which shifts with the tide
Ko Lao Lading and its overhanging cliff
Sheltered water when the Phi Phi route is rough
Halal meal and national park fees both included

fullDescription:
The four-island circuit on a longtail, departing after lunch so you arrive as everyone else is leaving.

Morning boats all leave Ao Nang within the same hour and reach the same beaches together. The afternoon departure inverts that. By the time you reach the later stops the moored fleet has gone, and Poda and Phra Nang are at their quietest of the day.

The Thale Waek sandbar is timed to work in your favour. The Separated Sea is a strip of sand linking Tup, Mor and Chicken islands that emerges as the tide drops and vanishes as it rises, so an afternoon trip on a falling tide walks out onto sand that was underwater when the morning boats passed it.

Chicken Island has the snorkelling: shallow coral just off the beach, close enough that you do not need to be a strong swimmer to see it. Phra Nang Cave Beach sits under an overhanging cliff on the Railay peninsula, with the shrine at one end where fishermen leave carved wooden offerings to a spirit they believe protects them at sea. The shrine is still in use, so it is worth being unobtrusive with photographs.

The longtail is slower and noisier than a speedboat and gets into shallow water a speedboat has to anchor away from, which on this route is the trade you want.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers round-trip hotel transfers, the longtail with guide, buffet lunch, snorkelling mask and fins, drinking water and soft drinks, fresh fruit, life jackets and insurance.

Six hours. National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Late departure that misses the morning fleet
Walk the Thale Waek sandbar as the tide drops
Snorkel shallow coral beside Chicken Island
Phra Nang Cave Beach and its working shrine
Longtail reaches water speedboats anchor away from

fullDescription:
An early start that covers both halves of Phang Nga Bay: the Hong Island group from Krabi, and the James Bond Island cluster further west.

Koh Tapu, the limestone needle that everyone calls James Bond Island, appeared in The Man with the Golden Gun in 1974 and has been the bay's most photographed rock ever since. It is genuinely striking, and it is also genuinely crowded by mid-morning, which is the argument for the early departure. Landing is restricted to protect the base of the rock, which has been eroding, so you view it from the adjacent beach rather than walking up to it.

Koh Panyi is the other half of that stop. It is a Muslim fishing village built almost entirely on stilts against a limestone cliff, founded by Javanese fishing families in the eighteenth century, with a mosque, a school and a floating football pitch that the village built itself after watching a World Cup.

Hong Beach and the national park waters around Koh Kudu Yai cover the Krabi side: the Hong lagoon, shallow green water inside limestone walls, and snorkelling where conditions allow.

Nine hours makes this a long day, and the early pickup is the point rather than an inconvenience.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers light breakfast, buffet lunch, unlimited soft drinks, seasonal fruit, tour insurance, a licensed guide and pickup and drop-off transfers.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Early departure, ahead of the mid-morning crowds
Koh Tapu, viewed from the beach rather than landed on
Koh Panyi, a stilt village with its own floating pitch
Hong lagoon and the national park waters
Breakfast, buffet lunch, licensed guide and transfers

fullDescription:
Phi Phi and the Krabi four islands in one speedboat day, front-loaded so Maya Bay comes before the fleet.

Maya Bay is the reason for the early start. The bay closed completely in 2018 after years of damage and reopened in 2022 under strict conditions: boats moor at the back of Phi Phi Leh and visitors walk in through the island, swimming inside the bay is restricted, and daily visitor numbers are capped. Arriving first means walking in rather than queueing, and seeing the bay closer to how it looks in the film it is famous for.

Pileh Lagoon follows, a deep channel of green water enclosed by cliffs on every side, then two separate reef systems for snorkelling, which is more than most Phi Phi trips manage. Lunch is a Thai buffet on Phi Phi Don, the inhabited island.

The return leg picks up Krabi's four islands, so the day covers both the famous offshore stop and the local circuit. That is a lot of ground for nine hours and a speedboat is the only way to do it, with the trade-off that speedboats pound in any chop.

We book with the operator directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers hotel pickup and drop-off in Ao Nang and Krabi Town, the speedboat with certified crew, an English-speaking guide, Thai buffet lunch, snorkel mask, fins and life jackets.

National park fees are collected at the pier unless confirmed otherwise, so carry cash. Nine hours, minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Maya Bay ahead of the day-trip fleet
Post-2022 rules: walk in, capped daily numbers
Pileh Lagoon, cliff-ringed on every side
Two separate reef systems for snorkelling
Phi Phi and the Krabi four islands in one day
